questions.stem: Which expression converts a mass concentration into a molar concentration?

options.explanation: The particle count plays no role in concentration units here.
g dm^-3 divided by g mol^-1 leaves mol dm^-3.
Multiplication would give g^2 mol^-1 dm^-3 - meaningless.
The 1000 factor converts cm^3 to dm^3, unrelated to mass-to-mole conversion.

options.explanation: That is the mass concentration wearing wrong units.

questions.stem: State the equation for molar concentration.
questions.modelAnswer: Molar concentration in mol dm^-3 = number of moles of solute / volume of solution in dm^3.

questions.stem: State the conversion between cm^3 and dm^3 used in concentration work.
questions.modelAnswer: 1 dm^3 = 1000 cm^3, so a volume in cm^3 is divided by 1000 to enter concentration equations in dm^3.

questions.stem: Explain why mixing up g dm^-3 and mol dm^-3 produces answers that are wrong by the molar-mass factor.
questions.modelAnswer: A mass concentration already contains grams per volume, while a molar concentration contains moles per volume; skipping the n = mass / molar mass step leaves the grams unconverted, so the numeric answer stays larger by exactly the molar mass in g mol^-1 while the units silently mismatch.

questions.stem: 6.34 g of NaCl end up dissolved in 250 cm^3 of solution. Calculate the molar concentration, using Mr(NaCl) = 58.5, to 3 s.f.
questions.modelAnswer: n = 6.34 / 58.5 gives 0.1084 mol; volume = 0.250 dm^3; c = 0.1084 mol over 0.250 dm^3 lands at 0.434 mol dm^-3.

options.explanation: That is not a trace amount at all.
One milligram in one cubic decimetre is the working definition.
A gram would be a thousand times too concentrated.
That is a thousand times too dilute.

options.text: The two volumes carry different units, so 152 cm^3 becomes 0.152 dm^3 before the ratio
options.explanation: ppm arithmetic requires matching units on top and bottom.

options.explanation: That is the raw fraction, unscaled.

questions.stem: Define 1 ppm in terms of mass and volume for aqueous solutions.
questions.modelAnswer: 1 ppm corresponds to 1 milligram dissolved in one cubic decimetre of water - equivalently 1 mg per kilogram, since that volume of water weighs a kilogram.

questions.stem: State what the v in ppmv denotes and the volume pair it compares.
questions.modelAnswer: The v marks concentration by volume: 1 ppmv means 1 cm^3 of the gas in 1 x 10^6 cm^3 (1000 dm^3) of air.

questions.stem: Explain why the identity of the gas is irrelevant when calculating an atmospheric concentration in ppm.
questions.modelAnswer: The ppm formula uses only the volume of the gas and the volume of the air, so the ratio depends on how much space the gas occupies, not on what the molecules are; the same 2.5 dm^3 in 10000 dm^3 of air is 250 ppm whether the gas is carbon dioxide or sulfur dioxide.

questions.stem: Calculate, in ppm, the gas concentration when 2.5 dm^3 of sulfur dioxide spreads through 4000 dm^3 of air, using the volume ratio.
questions.modelAnswer: ppm = (2.5 x 10^6) / 4000 = 625 ppm - the gas identity never enters the arithmetic.
